title: THE LAW AS MEANING ECONOMY Juridical Liquidation and the Semantic Architecture of Administered Justice
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
A legal-theoretical essay by Lee Sharks applying the Semantic Economy framework to administered justice.

The paper argues for a structural correspondence between AI summarization and juridical administration: both can tokenize lived complexity, strip context, relocate authorship into institutional voice, capture value, and close the record. It calls this sequence **juridical liquidation** and proposes a Juridical Liquidation Index for comparing what enters legal process with what survives into administrable form. The paper limits its target to dominant administrative modes and acknowledges restorative, abolitionist, participatory, and counter-juridical traditions. Its statutory readings, legal conclusions, license interpretations, formulas, and asserted homology are arguments of the essay, not settled doctrine, legal advice, or validated measurement.
